ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Cardiology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Progressive fatigue and shortness of breath during exertion with occasional palpitations and chest pounding when lying down

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
He also reports occasional palpitations and a sensation of pounding in his chest when lying down.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Marfan syndrome (FBN1 mutation)
- Thoracic aortic aneurysm (dilated aortic root, 4.2 cm)
- Chronic severe aortic regurgitation
- Mitral valve prolapse with mild regurgitation
- Ectopia lentis (bilateral lens subluxation)

He has no known chronic illnesses but has never undergone a formal physical exam.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Dental extraction with endocarditis prophylaxis (2020)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Metoprolol succinate 50 mg PO daily
- Lisinopril 10 mg PO daily
- Aspirin 81 mg PO daily

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father: Marfan syndrome, s/p prophylactic aortic root replacement (Bentall procedure) at age 38
- Paternal uncle: Sudden death at age 31 (presumed aortic dissection)
- Mother: Healthy, no connective tissue disorder
- Sibling: Younger sister with Marfan syndrome (under surveillance)

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Occasional (1-2 drinks per month). Occupation: Graduate student (Library Sciences).

VITAL SIGNS:
His blood pressure is 140/45 mm Hg and pulse is 90/min and bounding.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
His height is 193 cm (6’4”). His fingers are long and he has an arm span that exceeds his height. Cardiac auscultation reveals a murmur. Fundoscopic exam is normal.

PLAN:
An echocardiogram is ordered.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2021-01-15
Provider: Dr. Marcus Johnson, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Sudden visual changes in right eye after lightly rubbing it upon waking

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
This 27-year-old male with Marfan syndrome and bilateral lens subluxation, previously evaluated one year ago for aortic regurgitation, presents to the emergency department with a complaint of sudden visual changes in his right eye after lightly rubbing it upon waking up this morning. He denies any significant trauma or pain associated with the change.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Aortic Regurgitation (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Marfan syndrome (FBN1 mutation)
- Thoracic aortic aneurysm (dilated aortic root, 4.2 cm)
- Mitral valve prolapse with mild regurgitation
- Ectopia lentis (bilateral lens subluxation)

His past medical history is notable for tall stature, long extremities, and a recent diagnosis of mild mitral valve prolapse.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Dental extraction with endocarditis prophylaxis (2020)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Metoprolol succinate 50 mg PO daily
- Lisinopril 10 mg PO daily
- Aspirin 81 mg PO daily

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father: Marfan syndrome, s/p prophylactic aortic root replacement (Bentall procedure) at age 38
- Paternal uncle: Sudden death at age 31 (presumed aortic dissection)
- Mother: Healthy, no connective tissue disorder
- Sibling: Younger sister with Marfan syndrome (under surveillance)

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Occasional (1-2 drinks per month). Occupation: Graduate student (Library Sciences).

VITAL SIGNS:
His blood pressure is 130/70 mmHg, heart rate is 78 bpm

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, he is 6 feet 4 inches tall with an arm span that exceeds his height. Ocular examination reveals that the lens of the right eye is displaced superiorly and nasally. There is no evidence of redness, corneal abrasion, or conjunctival injection. Cardiac examination reveals a midsystolic click followed by a late systolic murmur at the apex. The rest of the examination is unremarkable.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2022-01-15
Provider: Dr. Priya Sharma, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Sudden, severe, tearing upper back pain at rest

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
This 28-year-old with Marfan syndrome and thoracic aortic aneurysm was seen in 2020 for aortic regurgitation and in 2021 for visual changes. He is brought to the emergency department after experiencing sudden, severe upper back pain that began while at rest, described as sharp and tearing.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Aortic Regurgitation (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Marfanoid habitus (diagnosed 2021-01-15)
- Marfan syndrome (FBN1 mutation)
- Thoracic aortic aneurysm (dilated aortic root, 4.2 cm)
- Mitral valve prolapse with mild regurgitation
- Ectopia lentis (bilateral lens subluxation)

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Dental extraction with endocarditis prophylaxis (2020)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Metoprolol succinate 50 mg PO daily
- Lisinopril 10 mg PO daily
- Aspirin 81 mg PO daily

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father: Marfan syndrome, s/p prophylactic aortic root replacement (Bentall procedure) at age 38
- Paternal uncle: Sudden death at age 31 (presumed aortic dissection)
- Mother: Healthy, no connective tissue disorder
- Sibling: Younger sister with Marfan syndrome (under surveillance)

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Occasional (1-2 drinks per month). Occupation: Graduate student (Library Sciences).

VITAL SIGNS:
His temperature is 36.7°C (98°F), blood pressure is 88/40 mm Hg in the right arm and 112/44 mm Hg in the left arm, and pulse is 112/min.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, he is tall and thin, with disproportionately long limbs and fingers. Cardiac auscultation reveals a high-pitched, early diastolic decrescendo murmur best heard at the left sternal border.

IMAGING:
A chest X-ray shows a widened mediastinum.
